items.original_text: Filing step: After the CUA is approved and becomes final (30-day appeal period), file the ABC license transfer application (person-to-person and premises-to-premises) with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control. What to say: Submit the ABC-220 transfer application, the executed purchase agreement, proof of the legal entity (Articles of Organization), the seller's permit from CDTFA, the lease for 995 Valencia, and the CUA approval (Motion and conditions). ABC will route the application to SFPD and SF Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm that the CUA covers the license. Pay the ABC transfer fee (roughly $1,000–$1,600). Post the ABC public notice at the premises for 30 days. If the tract is over-concentrated (28 active on-sale licenses against 12 authorized), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors or Planning; coordinate with Planning and your ABC broker to secure that letter before ABC completes its review.

items.original_text: Filing step: File for a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit with the San Francisco Entertainment Commission, after confirming with the Commission which permit the concept requires. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director with a description of the live entertainment (frequency, hours, amplified sound, performance area size) and ask whether the concept needs a Limited Live Performance permit (one performer, ending by 10 or 11 p.m., ≤ 200 sq ft) or a Place of Entertainment permit (primary entertainment use or later hours). If a POE is needed, submit the application online, pay the $2,708 fee (2026–27), schedule the intake meeting, complete the neighbor outreach, post the yellow notice for 30 days, and attend the Commission hearing (1st and 3rd Tuesdays). The application will be routed to Police, Planning (which will confirm the CUA covers entertainment), Public Health, and Fire. Commit to the Good Neighbor Policy, sound limits, and security plan in the application.

items.original_text: Filing step: File for a building permit with tenant improvements and change of use through the Department of Building Inspection, with plans stamped by an architect and routed to Planning, Public Health, Public Utilities Commission, and Fire. What to say: Hire an architect to prepare plans for the tenant improvements: kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, bar, seating, ADA upgrades, and finishes. Submit the building permit application through the PermitSF portal (most over-the-counter permits are online-only since September 14, 2026) with routing to Planning (for CUA conformance and change-of-use sign-off), DPH (for health plan check), PUC (for FOG grease interceptor), and Fire (for hood suppression and occupancy). The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation (budget $800–$15,000 depending on scope). Planning will not sign off until the CUA is final. DPH will assign a plan reviewer; submit the health plan check application ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant/bar in 2026–27) and schedule the pre-final and final inspections at least two weeks in advance.

items.original_text: Filing step: After the DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete, file for the Health Permit to Operate and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27; the annual license fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026–28). Ensure a certified food safety manager is on staff (submit the certificate with the application). Schedule the final DPH inspection for when the kitchen is complete, all equipment is installed, and hot water and hand sinks are operational. Failed inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 165 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $7,426 to $24,250. Notes: The timeline is the sum of days to approval for the four approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.health_permit), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.building_permit). These approvals run partly in parallel: the POE and building permit can be filed after the CUA is approved and final, and the health permit is filed after DPH plan check (which is part of the building permit routing) and construction are substantially complete. The CUA is the critical path (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, and hearing). The cost range is the sum of city and state government fees for those four approvals: CUA ($3,100–$15,000, higher if construction value is high or no fee waiver applies), POE or LLP permit ($612–$3,800, $2,708 for POE in 2026–27), health plan check and permit ($828 + $470 = $1,298 to $2,500 + $1,000 = $3,500), and building permit ($800–$15,000, percentage of construction valuation). It does not include the cost of purchasing and transferring the ABC Type 42 license (broker fees, license purchase price of tens of thousands of dollars, and ABC transfer fee of $1,000–$1,600), the architect's fees for plans, construction costs, or business setup fees (entity formation, EIN, business registration, seller's permit, food safety certification, RBS training, workers' comp insurance, music licenses). The ABC license transfer timeline (60–150 days per catalog:ca.abc_type_42) runs after CUA approval and is not included in the approval-path timeline above because it is a post-approval step, but it is a prerequisite to opening and serving alcohol. The overall time from CUA filing to opening is realistically 12–18 months if the CUA, POE, ABC transfer, building permit, and health inspections all proceed without delays.

items.original_text: Filing step: If Planning confirms a bar use and a CUA is required, form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State, obtain an EIN from the IRS, and register the San Francisco business with the Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization or corporation articles online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov ($70–$100), then apply for an EIN at irs.gov (free, same day). Within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco, register for a Business Registration Certificate at sftreasurer.org; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k). The Business Account Number (BAN) is needed for every other city permit, so do this immediately after forming the entity.

What to say: Engage a California ABC license broker to locate a Type 42 on-sale beer-wine public-premises license currently held by a bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (bounded roughly by 14th St, Potrero Ave, Cesar Chavez, and Dolores). Do not file the ABC transfer application until the CUA is approved by the Planning Commission and the 30-day appeal period has passed, because ABC will not issue the license without Planning sign-off. items.original_text: Filing step: File for a building permit with tenant improvements and change of use through the Department of Building Inspection, with plans stamped by an architect and routed to Planning, Public Health, Public Utilities Commission, and Fire. What to say: Hire an architect to prepare plans for the tenant improvements: kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, bar, seating, ADA upgrades, and finishes. Submit the building permit application through the PermitSF portal (most over-the-counter permits are online-only since September 14, 2026) with routing to Planning (for CUA conformance and change-of-use sign-off), DPH (for health plan check), PUC (for FOG grease interceptor), and Fire (for hood suppression and occupancy). The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation (budget $800–$15,000 depending on scope). Planning will not sign off until the CUA is final. DPH will assign a plan reviewer; submit the health plan check application ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant/bar in 2026–27) and schedule the pre-final and final inspections at least two weeks in advance.

items.original_text: Filing step: After the DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete, file for the Health Permit to Operate and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27; the annual license fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026–28). Ensure a certified food safety manager is on staff (submit the certificate with the application). Schedule the final DPH inspection for when the kitchen is complete, all equipment is installed, and hot water and hand sinks are operational. Failed inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection.

Notes: The timeline is the sum of days to approval for the four approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.health_permit), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.building_permit). These approvals run partly in parallel: the POE can be filed after the CUA is approved and final, and the health permit is filed after DPH plan check (which is part of the building permit routing) and construction are substantially complete. The CUA is the critical path (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, and hearing). The cost range is the sum of city and state government fees for those four approvals: CUA ($3,100–$15,000, higher if construction value is high or no fee waiver applies), POE or LLP permit ($2,708 for POE in 2026–27), health plan check and permit ($828 + $470 = $1,298 to $2,500 + $1,000 = $3,500), and building permit ($800–$15,000, percentage of construction valuation). It does not include the cost of purchasing and transferring the ABC Type 42 license (broker fees, license purchase price of tens of thousands of dollars, and ABC transfer fee of $1,000–$1,600), the architect's fees for plans, construction costs, or business setup fees (entity formation, EIN, business registration, seller's permit, food safety certification, RBS training, workers' comp insurance, music licenses). The ABC license transfer timeline (60–150 days per catalog:ca.abc_type_42) runs after CUA approval and is not included in the approval-path timeline above because it is a post-approval step, but it is a prerequisite to opening and serving alcohol.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: The ABC liquor license must be a license transferred from another bar located inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, not a new license or one transferred from outside the district. Basis: Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) requires a new bar in the SUD to use a license transferred from another bar within the district. This is a mandatory SUD requirement, not a discretionary condition, and applies to any bar use approval.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms a bar use and a CUA is required, form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State, obtain an EIN from the IRS, and register the San Francisco business with the Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: File LLC Articles of Organization or corporation articles online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov ($70–$100), then apply for an EIN at irs.gov (free, same day). Within 30 days of starting business in San Francisco, register for a Business Registration Certificate at sftreasurer.org; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g., $55 up to $100k). The Business Account Number (BAN) is needed for every other city permit, so do this immediately after forming the entity.

outcomes.original: Filing step: In parallel with the CUA, identify and negotiate to acquire an ABC Type 42 beer-wine bar license from another bar located inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. What to say: Engage a California ABC license broker to locate a Type 42 on-sale beer-wine public-premises license currently held by a bar inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (bounded roughly by 14th St, Potrero Ave, Cesar Chavez, and Dolores). Negotiate the purchase price and escrow terms. Do not file the ABC transfer application until the CUA is approved by the Planning Commission and the 30-day appeal period has passed, because ABC will not issue the license without Planning sign-off. Budget 90–150 days for the ABC transfer process after CUA approval, including the 30-day public posting at 995 Valencia, ABC investigation, and possible Public Convenience or Necessity review if the tract is over-concentrated.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the CUA is approved and becomes final (30-day appeal period), file the ABC license transfer application (person-to-person and premises-to-premises) with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control. What to say: Submit the ABC-220 transfer application, the executed purchase agreement, proof of the legal entity (Articles of Organization), the seller's permit from CDTFA, the lease for 995 Valencia, and the CUA approval (Motion and conditions). ABC will route the application to SFPD and SF Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm that the CUA covers the license. Pay the ABC transfer fee (roughly $1,000–$1,600). Post the ABC public notice at the premises for 30 days. If the tract is over-concentrated (28 active on-sale licenses against 12 authorized), ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors or Planning; coordinate with Planning and your ABC broker to secure that letter before ABC completes its review.
outcomes.note: The record states only the fee range ($1,000–$1,600); it does not state the filing timing, form number, required documents, routing, posting requirements, or concentration numbers.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File for a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit with the San Francisco Entertainment Commission, after confirming with the Commission which permit the concept requires. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director with a description of the live entertainment (frequency, hours, amplified sound, performance area size) and ask whether the concept needs a Limited Live Performance permit (one performer, ending by 10 or 11 p.m., ≤ 200 sq ft) or a Place of Entertainment permit (primary entertainment use or later hours). If a POE is needed, submit the application online, pay the $2,708 fee (2026–27), schedule the intake meeting, complete the neighbor outreach, post the yellow notice for 30 days, and attend the Commission hearing (1st and 3rd Tuesdays). The application will be routed to Police, Planning (which will confirm the CUA covers entertainment), Public Health, and Fire. Commit to the Good Neighbor Policy, sound limits, and security plan in the application.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File for a building permit with tenant improvements and change of use through the Department of Building Inspection, with plans stamped by an architect and routed to Planning, Public Health, Public Utilities Commission, and Fire. What to say: Hire an architect to prepare plans for the tenant improvements: kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, bar, seating, ADA upgrades, and finishes. Submit the building permit application through the PermitSF portal (most over-the-counter permits are online-only since September 14, 2026) with routing to Planning (for CUA conformance and change-of-use sign-off), DPH (for health plan check), PUC (for FOG grease interceptor), and Fire (for hood suppression and occupancy). The building permit fee is a percentage of construction valuation (budget $800–$15,000 depending on scope). Planning will not sign off until the CUA is final. DPH will assign a plan reviewer; submit the health plan check application ($828–$2,207 for a new restaurant/bar in 2026–27) and schedule the pre-final and final inspections at least two weeks in advance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete, file for the Health Permit to Operate and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27; the annual license fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026–28). Ensure a certified food safety manager is on staff (submit the certificate with the application). Schedule the final DPH inspection for when the kitchen is complete, all equipment is installed, and hot water and hand sinks are operational. Failed inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 165 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $7,426 to $24,250. Notes: The timeline is the sum of days to approval for the four approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.health_permit), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.building_permit). These approvals run partly in parallel: the POE and building permit can be filed after the CUA is approved and final, and the health permit is filed after DPH plan check (which is part of the building permit routing) and construction are substantially complete. The CUA is the critical path (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, and hearing). The cost range is the sum of city and state government fees for those four approvals: CUA ($3,100–$15,000, higher if construction value is high or no fee waiver applies), POE or LLP permit ($612–$3,800, $2,708 for POE in 2026–27), health plan check and permit ($828 + $470 = $1,298 to $2,500 + $1,000 = $3,500), and building permit ($800–$15,000, percentage of construction valuation). It does not include the cost of purchasing and transferring the ABC Type 42 license (broker fees, license purchase price of tens of thousands of dollars, and ABC transfer fee of $1,000–$1,600), the architect's fees for plans, construction costs, or business setup fees (entity formation, EIN, business registration, seller's permit, food safety certification, RBS training, workers' comp insurance, music licenses). The ABC license transfer timeline (60–150 days per catalog:ca.abc_type_42) runs after CUA approval and is not included in the approval-path timeline above because it is a post-approval step, but it is a prerequisite to opening and serving alcohol. The overall time from CUA filing to opening is realistically 12–18 months if the CUA, POE, ABC transfer, building permit, and health inspections all proceed without delays.
